title: The US–Japan chip war of the 1980s: 100% tariffs, a secret 20% target, and Korea's win
short: The 1980s US–Japan chip war, and why Korea won it
dek: In 1987 Washington slapped 100% tariffs on Japanese electronics to enforce a chip deal. Japan did open its market, but the real winner of the fight was a country that wasn't in it.
card: Japan held 75% of the world memory-chip market in 1987. By 2001 it had 20%, and Korea had 40%.
